item.title: Could Texas Still Secede? Some Haven't Given Up the Fight
item.description: Though there's no legal off-ramp from the United States — or is there? — Texas secessionists and fellow travelers insist the dream is still alive and well — and winnable.

item.title: BioNTX CEO Kathleen Rosenblum Retires; Gina Ford Named New Chief Executive
item.description: North Texas bioscience organization announces retirement of Kathleen Rosenblum and appointment of Gina Ford, effective March 2.

item.title: Royal Cup to Acquire Fort Worth-Based Farmer Brothers in All-Cash Deal
item.description: The transaction would combine two coffee companies with nearly 250 years of industry experience and expand Royal Cup’s national reach across foodservice and retail markets.

item.title: Fort Worth Weighing Incentives for $1.1B Edged Data Center at Veale Ranch
item.description: City officials say the project would bring a $1.1 billion capital investment, 50 technical jobs and nearly $50 million in net new tax revenue over a decade.

item.title: Justin Brands Wins Two Honors at Fort Worth American Advertising Awards
item.description: Fort Worth-based Justin Brands earned a Crystal Award for its Team Justin Rodeo Athletes campaign and a Silver Addy for Tony Lama’s Día de los Muertos campaign at the American Advertising Awards hosted by AAF Fort Worth.

item.title: Texas Wesleyan Begins Final Construction Phase on Karen Cramer Stadium
item.description: Seating and press box construction mark the final stage of a multi-year project that will anchor a new athletics corridor and support Texas Wesleyan’s planned move to NCAA Division II.

item.title: Fort Worth-Based HTeaO Adds Two Executives as Franchise Chain Prepares for 40 New Stores in 2026
item.description: Fort Worth-based iced tea franchise HTeaO has appointed Jerry McClain and Brian Aga to key leadership roles as the company prepares for more than 40 new store openings in 2026.

item.title: Manny Ramirez: Lower the Temperature in Politics and Return to Results
item.description: In a time of political polarization and viral outrage, Tarrant County Commissioner Manny Ramirez argues that real leadership is measured by competence, civility, and results that strengthen communities.

item.title: Presidio Begins Trading on NYSE as $735M Fort Worth Oil and Gas Company
item.description: Fort Worth-based Presidio Production Co. launches as a public company after completing its business combination with EQV Ventures Acquisition Corp.

item.title: $1.7B Westside Village Development Breaks Ground Near Fort Worth Cultural District
item.description: The 37-acre project near the Cultural District will bring offices, retail, housing, and a hotel to the former Fort Worth ISD headquarters site.
